hints: Focus on what each starting material needs to become a $\text{-COOH}$ group, and remember oxidation stops at different places for different alcohol classes.
Check statement 1 first. A primary alcohol can go all the way to a carboxylic acid, but a secondary alcohol stops at a ketone.
Now link the other two routes. Think about adding water across $\text{-C}\equiv\text{N}$ and splitting an ester with dilute acid to see which acid fragment forms.
walkthrough:
**Test statement 1 - oxidation of alcohols**

Think about how many hydrogens are on the carbon with the $\text{-OH}$ group. Only primary alcohols have enough to reach the carboxylic acid stage.

$$\text{RCH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{RCHO} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{RCOOH}$$

**Why secondary alcohols cannot do this**

A secondary alcohol oxidises to a ketone, and the C-C bonds do not break under normal oxidising conditions, so no carboxylic acid forms.

$$\text{R}_2\text{CHOH} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{R}_2\text{C=O (ketone, stops here)}$$

**Test statement 2 - hydrolysis of nitriles**

This is a standard two carbon chain extension route. Acid hydrolysis adds water across the nitrile to give the acid plus ammonium ions.

$$\text{RC}\equiv\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Test statement 3 - acid hydrolysis of ethyl propanoate**

Acid hydrolysis splits the ester at the single bond to oxygen. The acyl part becomes the carboxylic acid and the alkyl part becomes the alcohol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{HCl}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Combine the verdicts**

Statement 1 is false, while statements 2 and 3 are both true. So the correct combination is 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes statement 1. This option claims all three statements are correct, but secondary alcohols oxidise only to ketones, not to carboxylic acids.
options.B: Incorrect because it includes statement 1 and excludes statement 3. Statement 1 is false, while statement 3 is true since ethyl propanoate hydrolyses to propanoic acid and ethanol.
options.C: Correct because only statements 2 and 3 are true. Nitriles hydrolyse to carboxylic acids, and ethyl propanoate gives propanoic acid on acid hydrolysis, while statement 1 is false.
options.D: Incorrect because it selects statement 1 only. Statement 1 is the false one, as only primary alcohols (with reflux and strong oxidant) give carboxylic acids.
